title: The Honest Wrecker
openingText: Marrow has a lantern he does not need, an honest face he uses professionally, and a stair cut into the cliff that is a great deal better swept than a smuggler's stair ought to be. 'Everything on this coast came off a ship,' he says. 'The only question anybody sensible asks is whose turn it is.'
dialogueWalkaway: Suit yourself. Mind the strand on the way out. It comes up faster than a walk.
dialogueAccept: Handsomely done. Come back on a spring tide and ask for me by name.
confidence: That beach is promised to somebody else on the same night.

clauses.text: Marrow's real tide-tables, the ones the charts get wrong twice a day.
A customary share of the season's tide-line. Coin, no questions.
A beach nobody watches, for one landing, at a time of your choosing.
You walk the cliff path with him one night. You do not have to like it.
The gap in the patrol rota, and the hour it opens
You carry a small sealed package two towns on
